sections.h2: How can I sell my house fast in Wausau, Wisconsin?
sections.html:
The fastest sales in Wausau come from buyers who do not depend on a mortgage, because loan approval and appraisal are the steps that stretch a listing out. You can also list with an agent or sell the house yourself. All three paths end the same way: a condition report to the buyer, an electronic transfer return, and a deed recorded at the Marathon County Register of Deeds.

Wausau is the county seat of Marathon County and sits on the Wisconsin River in central Wisconsin. The Census Bureau estimates 40,188 residents as of July 1, 2025, up 0.5 percent from the 39,994 counted in 2020. The wider Wausau metropolitan area, which is all of Marathon County, had 138,013 people in 2020.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about the city of Wausau?
sections.html:
Wausau grew up around logging. The Wisconsin River drew settlers in the mid-1800s, a sawmill opened in 1840, the settlement became a town by 1852, a village in 1861, and a chartered city in 1872. The railroad arrived in 1874, and by 1906 the pine was gone, so the economy shifted toward other industries, with Employers Insurance of Wausau, now part of Liberty Mutual, leading the diversification. Hmong refugees began arriving at the end of the 1970s, and Census data show 10.4 percent of residents identify as Asian alone today.

The layout is easy to explain to an out-of-town buyer. The river splits the city into east and west, with numbered streets on the east side and numbered avenues on the west side. Grand Avenue becomes North 6th Street as it enters downtown, and Business 51 follows the old route of US 51 through town. The Census Bureau counts 19.22 square miles of land.

  • Schools. The Wausau School District runs 14 elementary schools, John Muir and Horace Mann middle schools, and Wausau East and Wausau West high schools. The D.C. Everest Area School District also serves a large part of the Wausau area, so check which district a particular address belongs to.
  • Recreation. Rib Mountain State Park, Granite Peak Ski Area, the Leigh Yawkey Woodson Art Museum and the Grand Theater are the attractions the city is known for.
  • Jobs. Nearly a third of the Marathon County economy is manufacturing, with paper, insurance, home manufacturing and tourism among the prominent industries.
  • Transit and air. Metro Ride provides local buses, and Central Wisconsin Airport offers commercial flights with American Eagle and Delta Connection.
  • Nearby communities. Schofield, Weston, Mosinee, Maine, Rib Mountain, Kronenwetter and Rothschild form the suburban ring.

sections.html:
Wausau homes are priced well below the figures seen in Milwaukee-area suburbs. The Census Bureau reports a median owner-occupied value of $167,900 for 2020 to 2024, with 57.6 percent of housing units owner-occupied. The table below pulls the main figures from QuickFacts.

sections.h2: What does Wisconsin require when I sell a Wausau house?
sections.html:
If the property has one to four dwelling units, you must give the buyer a completed real estate condition report no later than 10 days after the contract is accepted. Under chapter 709 of the Wisconsin Statutes, a buyer who does not receive it can rescind within two business days after the 10 days run out and recover any deposit. Personal representatives, trustees and court-appointed fiduciaries who never occupied the home do not have to complete it.

The grantor also pays a transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value under s. 77.22, or $3 per $1,000, collected when the deed is recorded. A Wausau home sold for $170,000 would owe $510. Both grantor and grantee sign the electronic return, and transfers by will, descent or survivorship are among those exempted by s. 77.25.

sections.h2: How do property taxes and assessments work in Wausau?
sections.html:
Wausau taxes are due in full by January 31 or in installments on January 31, April 30 and July 31, and special assessment charges on the bill must be paid in full by January 31. The city clerk's office handles these payments directly, and Marathon County says payments for the City of Wausau are not made to the county. Pay online through ePayments, by ACH, at participating banks until July 31, in the drop boxes at City Hall on Grant Street or across from the post office on Forest Street, by mail, or in person at 407 Grant Street between 8:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. A returned electronic payment carries a $45 fee.

The Assessment Department at 715-261-6600 values property under chapter 70 of the Wisconsin Statutes at the full value obtainable in a private sale. The city's last revaluation was as of January 1, 2020, and the state compares assessments to sales to see whether the citywide ratio stays between 90 and 110 percent of market value. You get a mailed notice when your assessment changes, and the Open Book period lets you meet an appraiser before any formal appeal.

Sellers who are behind on taxes may find help close to home. Marathon County lists a 5x5 short-term loan of up to $5,000 for taxes that are three years or more past due, open to applicants who are 55 or older or disabled, with a $3 monthly service charge. Call the county at 715-261-1150 to ask about eligibility.

sections.h2: Which Wausau city rules matter before I list?
sections.html:
Property maintenance and rental rules are the two areas most likely to affect a sale. The Inspections and Zoning division, at 407 Grant Street and 715-261-6780, handles complaints and permits. Its rules cover trash containers, parked vehicles and yard signs, and a buyer's agent walking the property will notice any violation.

  • Trash and recycling carts may go out no sooner than 3:00 p.m. the day before pickup and must be removed by 11:00 a.m. the day after. Between pickups they belong in a garage, shed, or behind or beside the house.
  • Vehicles may be parked only on hard-surfaced driveway areas, not on the grass. Inoperative or unlicensed vehicles are not allowed on residential lots.
  • Boats, trailers, campers and similar equipment cannot sit in a required front yard or corner side yard except on a hard-surfaced driveway, and anything over 30 feet must be in an enclosed structure.
  • Zoning allows two yard signs at a time, each no larger than 6 square feet and 4 feet high. Real estate signs cannot be placed on boulevards, public right-of-way or utility poles.

If the house is a rental, the division's rental properties page lists rental registration, rental licensing and inspection, and a rent abatement program. Ask the division which of those apply to your unit before you transfer it.

sections.h2: How do I record the deed in Marathon County?
sections.html:
Mail the original deed, the electronic transfer return receipt and the recording fee to the Register of Deeds at 500 Forest Street, Wausau. The fee is $30 per document, and any transfer fee is paid at the same time. Since January 1, 2026 the office returns recorded documents electronically unless you include a self-addressed, stamped envelope, so write your email address on the submission.

The county cannot give legal advice. A title company or an attorney commonly prepares the deed. The recorded-document certification fee is $1 and copies cost $2 for the first page and $1 for each additional page.

sections.h2: Which selling route suits my Wausau house?
sections.html:
Compare the routes on timing and net cash, and write the figures down.

  • List with an agent. Reaches the widest pool of buyers if the house shows well and you can wait for financing.
  • Sell on your own. Keeps more of the price but puts the disclosures, signs and contract on you.
  • Accept a cash offer. Fits an inherited house, a rental with tenants, a house with deferred repairs, or a seller on a short clock. Ask for the number in writing and for who pays title and recording costs.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Wausau?
faqs.a: The Marathon County Register of Deeds charges $30 per document, plus any real estate transfer fee shown on the electronic return receipt. Copies are $2 for the first page and $1 for each additional page. Documents go to 500 Forest Street, Wausau.

faqs.q: When are Wausau property taxes due?
faqs.a: Pay in full by January 31, or in installments due January 31, April 30 and July 31. Special assessment charges on the bill must be paid in full by January 31. The City of Wausau collects these payments, not Marathon County.

faqs.q: Do I have to give a buyer a condition report in Wausau?
faqs.a: Yes, for one-to-four unit homes. Wis. Stat. chapter 709 requires the completed report within 10 days after the contract is accepted. A buyer who does not get it may rescind within two business days after that period, unless you are an exempt fiduciary who never lived in the home.

faqs.q: Can I put a for-sale sign in my Wausau yard?
faqs.a: Yes, on your own property. Zoning allows two yard signs at one time, each up to 6 square feet and 4 feet tall. Signs cannot be placed on boulevards, other public right-of-way or utility poles.

faqs.q: What is the Wisconsin transfer fee on a Wausau sale?
faqs.a: The grantor pays 30 cents per $100 of value, which is $3 per $1,000, when the deed is recorded. A $170,000 sale would owe $510. Transfers by will, descent or survivorship are exempt under s. 77.25.
